record.title: The linked-pairs dimension-dropping conjecture
record.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a graph. A pair of vertices is **linked** in $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^k$ when its distance is fixed across all generic equivalent realizations, and **globally linked** when that distance is fixed across all equivalent realizations. **The linked-pairs dimension-dropping conjecture.** If $\{u,v\}$ is linked in $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$, then $\{u,v\}$ is globally linked in $G$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. This would clarify the relationship between rigidity in consecutive dimensions and would imply the paper's dimension-dropping theorem and a strengthening of its minimally globally rigid graph theorem. The conjecture is proved in the cases $d=1,2$ but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi and Tibor Jordán, “Minimally globally rigid graphs”, arXiv:2202.11617 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11617

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2022).

record.title: The determinant formula for the reduced walk matrix of the Dynkin graph $D_n$
record.statement:
Let $D_n$ ($n\ge 4$) be the Dynkin graph, let $W(D_n)$ be its walk matrix, and let $\hat{W}(D_n)$ be the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix obtained from $W(D_n)$ by removing the first row and the last column. **Determinant conjecture.** The determinant satisfies

$$
\det \hat{W}(D_n)=
\begin{cases}
\pm 2^{\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor-1} & \text{if }4\nmid n,\\
0 & \text{if }4\mid n.
\end{cases}
$$

The paper presents this formula as a conjecture and proves it, thereby confirming a recent conjecture of Wang, Liu, and Wang concerning the walk matrix of $D_n$.
record.source_name: Wei Wang, Chuanming Wang and Songlin Guo, “On the walk matrix of the Dynkin graph D_n”, arXiv:2202.13279 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13279

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Dual Lieb–Thirring conjecture for the kinetic-energy constant
record.statement:
Let $K_d$ be the optimal constant in the kinetic-energy inequality referred to as equation (kinetic), and let $K_d^{\mathrm{one}}$ and $K_d^{\mathrm{cl}}$ be the corresponding one-particle and semiclassical constants. **Dual Lieb–Thirring conjecture for $\gamma=1$.** The optimal constant is

$$
K_d=\begin{cases}
K_d^{\mathrm{one}},&d\leq2,\\
K_d^{\mathrm{cl}},&d\geq3.
\end{cases}
$$

By the stated duality, the same assertion also gives the optimal constants in the associated alternative kinetic-energy formulations. The conjecture is presented as the dual formulation of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture at $\gamma=1$; the supplied text does not state a resolution of this formulation.
record.source_name: Lukas Schimmer, “The state of the Lieb–Thirring conjecture”, arXiv:2203.06051 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.06051

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2022). “The conjecture has been proved for $\gamma=1/2$ and $\gamma\ge3/2$ but remains open in the parameter range $1/2<\gamma<3/2$.”

record.title: Dorpalen-Barry et al.'s homology conjecture for $U$-nucleus complexes
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected undirected simple graph with at least $3$ vertices, and let $U\subseteq V(G)$. Define the $U$-nucleus complex by

$$
\Delta^{G}_{U}=\{E(G)\setminus E(N):N\in\mathcal{N}(G),\ U\subseteq V(N)\},
$$

where $\mathcal{N}(G)$ is the set of nuclei of $G$. **Dorpalen-Barry et al.'s homology conjecture.** The reduced homology group $\tilde{H}_k(\Delta^{G}_{U};\mathbb{R})$ is nonzero only if either $U=\emptyset$ and $k=|E(G)|-|V(G)|-1$, or $|U|>1$ and $k=|E(G)|-|V(G)|$. This conjecture concerns the homological concentration of the complexes used to prove Elser's conjecture; the supplied source describes it as a conjecture posed by Dorpalen-Barry et al., while the present paper's abstract says that it is proved there.
record.source_name: Apratim Chakraborty, Anupam Mondal, Sajal Mukherjee and Kuldeep Saha, “On Elser's conjecture and the topology of U-nucleus complex”, arXiv:2203.12525 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.12525

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Klivans's uniqueness conjecture for sandpile torsor structures on plane graphs
record.statement: Let $(G,\chi)$ be a plane graph, meaning a planar graph equipped with a plane ribbon structure. A **sandpile torsor structure** assigns a free transitive action of the sandpile group $\operatorname{Pic}^0(G)$ to the spanning trees $\mathcal T(G)$, independently of a choice of sink vertex. **Klivans's conjecture.** For plane graphs, there is only one sandpile torsor structure. The conjecture is motivated by the equivalence of the Bernardi and rotor-routing algorithms on plane graphs; in this paper, the authors make the notion precise through consistency and prove that there are exactly four consistent algorithms, all having the same structure as rotor-routing, thereby resolving the conjecture.
record.source_name: Ankan Ganguly and Alex McDonough, “Rotor-Routing Induces the Only Consistent Sandpile Torsor Structure on Plane Graphs”, arXiv:2203.15079 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.15079

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2022). “This conjecture was independently proven by Ding as well as by Shokrieh and Wright . } However, both algorithms satisfy , and they both define the same sandpile torsor algorithm .”

record.title: Maximality conjecture for the $(\mathbb{F}_q,\alpha)$ and $(\alpha\mathbb{F}_q,1)$ constructions
record.statement:
Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $m\geq 2$ satisfy $m\mid (q+1)/2$, and consider the cliques in $\mathrm{GP}(q^2,m)$ produced by the $(\mathbb F_q,\alpha)$-construction and the $(\alpha\mathbb F_q,1)$-construction. **Maximality conjecture.** If

$$
p\nmid(m-1)\qquad\text{and}\qquad 2\leq m\leq \frac{q+1}{3},
$$

then both cliques are maximal. The claim generalises the known maximality result for the corresponding constructions in Paley graphs, while the extension to generalised Paley graphs is stated under these additional assumptions.
record.source_name: Sergey Goryainov, Leonid Shalaginov and Chi Hoi Yip, “On eigenfunctions and maximal cliques of generalised Paley graphs of square order”, arXiv:2203.16081 (2022).

record.title: Connectivity conjecture for rigidity of abstract simplicial complexes
record.statement: Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $G$ be the graph of an abstract simplicial $(d+1)$-complex. **Connectivity conjecture.** If $G$ is $(2d-1)$-connected, then $G$ is rigid in $\mathbb R^d$. The bound is best possible, and the conjecture holds for $d=1$ and $d=2$. The source also reports that its hypotheses imply $C^1_2$-cofactor rigidity, which is conjectured to coincide with rigidity in $\mathbb R^3$; the general case remains open.
record.source_name: James Cruickshank, Bill Jackson and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Global Rigidity of Triangulated Manifolds”, arXiv:2204.02503 (2024).

record.title: Reality conjecture for trees in prime graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a tree associated with a simple module $L_q(\boldsymbol{\pi})$ over a quantum affine algebra, and call $G$ **real** when the tensor square of $L_q(\boldsymbol{\pi})$ is simple.

**Reality conjecture for trees.** Every tree is real.

This conjecture concerns the relationship between finite-dimensional representations of quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras. The source gives no resolution or evidence establishing the conjecture, so its status remains open.

record.title: The nonexistence conjecture for M-property incidence graphs of 2-quasi-symmetric designs
record.statement:
Let a **2-quasi-symmetric design** be a $2$-design whose distinct blocks intersect in either $x$ or $y$ points, and consider its point-line incidence graph. The parameter $x$ is the smaller intersection number of distinct blocks.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** There are no point-line incidence graphs of a $2$-quasi-symmetric design with $x=0$ that have the $M$-property.

This conjecture concerns the classification of distance-regularised graphs with the $M$-property. Existing quasi-symmetric $2$-designs with $x=0$ do not satisfy the relevant condition, but the general nonexistence claim remains open.

record.title: Hibi–Tsuchiya's conjecture on the h-vector of cycle graph stable set Ehrhart rings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cycle graph with $\ell\geq 3$, let $R=E_{\mathbb{K}}[\operatorname{STAB}(G)]$ be its Ehrhart ring, and write its h-vector as $(h_0,h_1,\ldots,h_s)$ with $h_s\neq 0$. Since $\dim R=2\ell+2$ and $a(R)=-3$, one has $s=2\ell-1$. **Hibi–Tsuchiya's conjecture.** The h-vector of $R$ has the form

$$
(1,h_1,h_2,\ldots,h_{\ell-1},h_{\ell-1}+(-1)^{\ell-1},h_{\ell-2}+(-1)^{\ell-2},\ldots,h_3-1,h_2+1,h_1,1).
$$

The conjecture concerns the symmetry and alternating correction terms in the h-vector of the Ehrhart ring of a cycle graph. The source states that Hibi and Tsuchiya made this conjecture and that it is proved in the paper.
record.source_name: Mitsuhiro Miyazaki, “Non-Gorenstein locus and almost Gorenstein property of the Ehrhart ring of the stable set polytope of a cycle graph”, arXiv:2205.01409 (2022).
record.references:

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Felsner–Hurtado–Noy–Streinu conjecture for simple great-circle arrangements
record.statement:
An arrangement of great-circles is a collection of great-circles on the sphere, and its arrangement graph has a vertex at each intersection point and edges given by the circle segments between consecutive intersection points. The arrangement is **simple** when no three great-circles pass through the same point.

**Felsner–Hurtado–Noy–Streinu conjecture.** The arrangement graph of every simple arrangement of great-circles on the sphere is 3-colorable.

This conjecture concerns the colorability of arrangement graphs; the paper proves it for the subclass of triangle-saturated great-pseudocircle arrangements, while the general case remains open.

record.title: The principal-polynomial support-reduction conjecture
record.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of the paper's supported-subset definition, including $(a,b,m,n)\in\mathcal{Q}$ and the associated objects $S,E^\circ,F^\circ,\alpha^\circ$. Fix $\ell\in[\mathrm{u}_F,\mathrm{v}_F]$, and let $P_1$ be the projection to the quotient by $L$. Suppose that $B$ is supported with respect to $(S,E^\circ,F^\circ,\alpha^\circ)$ and that $P_1(x_j)=0$ for $j\in[\ell+1,\mathrm{v}_F]$.

**The principal-polynomial support-reduction conjecture.** If $E^\circ$ is a principal polynomial, then either

$$
P_1(x_\ell)=0
$$

or there exists a proper subset of $B$ supported with respect to $(S,E^\circ,F^\circ,\alpha^\circ)$.

The source states that this conjecture implies the Jacobian conjecture. Its resolution status is not supplied.

record.title: Thompson's conjecture on derangements of primitive permutation groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite primitive permutation group on a set $\Omega$. A **derangement** is a fixed-point-free element of $G$.

**Thompson's conjecture.** For any two distinct elements $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\Omega$, there exists a derangement $g\in G$ such that $\alpha^g=\beta$.

This conjecture concerns the distribution of derangements in finite primitive permutation groups and is mentioned as a related problem; the supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

record.title: The Hessenberg variety homeomorphism conjecture for smooth permutations
record.statement:
Let $SL_n(\mathbb{C})$ be the special linear group, let $X\in SL_n(\mathbb{C})$ be regular semisimple, and let $w\in S_n$ be smooth. Denote by $\mathcal{Y}_w(X)$ the variety associated to $w$ and $X$ in the paper, and call a permutation **codominant** according to the paper's definition.

**Hessenberg variety homeomorphism conjecture.** There exists a codominant permutation $w'$ such that

$$
\mathcal{Y}_w(X)\text{ and }\mathcal{Y}_{w'}(X)\text{ are homeomorphic}.
$$

The paper describes this as a strengthening of an earlier theorem, but the supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Alex Abreu and Antonio Nigro, “An update on Haiman's conjectures”, arXiv:2206.00073 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: Delanoy's descent-set criterion for zircons in types A, D and E
record.statement:
Let $[u,w]$ be a Bruhat interval in a Weyl group of type $A$, $D$, or $E$. Write $D_L(w)$ for the left descent set of $w$, namely the set of simple reflections $s$ such that $sw<w$. A **zircon** is a Bruhat interval with the corresponding compression property. **Delanoy's descent-set conjecture.** There exists $s\in D_L(w)$ such that either

$$
sw\not\geq u,
$$

or

$$
su>u.
$$

Delanoy's conjecture is stated to imply the zircon-to-lower-interval conjecture above. The paper presents these conjectures as open and reports verification of its related conjectures in types $A_n$ for $n\leq 8$.
record.source_name: Vincent Umutabazi, “Zircons and smooth Bruhat intervals in symmetric groups”, arXiv:2206.06538 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06538

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2022). “Note that Conjecture is false in multiply laced types.”

record.title: The homomorphism-threshold conjecture for simply connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simply connected graph and fix $r\geq 2$. Suppose $\phi:G\to H$ is a graph homomorphism such that $H$ is $C_{2r+1}$-free, and suppose further that some odd cycle $C$ of $G$ satisfies

$$
|\phi(V(C))|\leq 2r+2.
$$

**Homomorphism-threshold conjecture.** Then

$$
\chi(G)\leq 2r.
$$

This conjecture proposes an improved bound on the chromatic number in the setting of the paper's homomorphism-threshold theorem. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Maya Sankar, “Homotopy and the Homomorphism Threshold of Odd Cycles”, arXiv:2206.07525 (2022).

record.title: Existence of an infinite bounded non-lattice with a Dacey orthogonality space
record.statement: Let $P$ be a bounded poset, and let $(Q^+(P),\perp)$ denote the orthogonality space associated with $P$. A poset is **Dacey** when every maximal orthogonal subset of $Q^+(P)$ is a base for the corresponding orthogonality space. **Existence conjecture.** There exists an infinite bounded non-lattice $P$ such that $(Q^+(P),\perp)$ is Dacey. The preceding results establish lattice-theoretic properties of the orthogonality spaces associated with bounded posets, but do not settle whether the Dacey property can occur for an infinite bounded poset that is not a lattice.

record.title: 5-cycle double cover Conjecture for bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph. A **$5$-cycle double cover** is a multiset of five cycles in $G$ such that every edge $e\in E(G)$ belongs to exactly two members of the multiset. **5-cycle double cover Conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a $5$-cycle double cover. This is one of the standard cycle-cover conjectures for bridgeless cubic graphs and is discussed in the source alongside the Fan–Raspaud and Berge–Fulkerson conjectures.

record.title: The polygonal-digraph endpoint characterization conjecture
record.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be an unweighted polygonal digraph of order $n\geq 2$, and let $\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)$ denote its Laplacian spread. A $k$-imploding star is the digraph family named in the source. **The polygonal-digraph endpoint characterization conjecture.** If $\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)\in\{0,1\}$, then $\Gamma$ is a regular digraph or a $k$-imploding star. In particular, if $\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)=0$, then $\Gamma$ is a regular tournament or a $k$-imploding star; if $\operatorname{sp}(\Gamma)=1$, then $n\geq 4$ is even and $\Gamma$ or $\overline{\Gamma}$ is an $\frac{n-2}{2}$-regular digraph. The conjecture is based on empirical data and is stated as open.

record.statement: Let the Laplacian spread of a digraph be bounded by the bound referred to in the source as equation (unwght-spread-bound). **The linear-slope-one bound conjecture.** That bound can be reduced to a linear function of $n$ with slope $1$.
